differences.what: the round tower: the photograph's stands on the 18th Street flank about 8 m back from the front, where the 1911 sheet draws a bump in the north wall, its eaves about 12.9 m and its cone to about 18.7 m; the draft put it at the front's north-west corner under an eave about 16 m up
differences.how: T-2538: the tower stood at u 12.6 on the flank, 1.1 m proud as the sheet draws it, eaves 12.9 m, cone 5.8 m; its axis within about 20 px of the photograph's x 698, its apex within about 25 px; T-2843: carried onto K01 as a K08 tower on the 18th Street wall, axis u 12.6, r 1.45 m, its centre 0.1 m out of the wall, eaves 12.9 m, cone to about 18.8 m; its apex within about 20 px of the photograph's

differences.what: the main block's height: two storeys of wall to a heavy cornice at about 8.1 m (principal floor 1.45 m up a stair of nine risers), the third storey in the roof; the draft stood three full storeys to an eave at about 12 m
differences.how: T-2538: principal floor 1.45 m, storeys 3.55 and 3.1 m to the cornice at 8.1 m; T-2843: K01's principal floor 1.45 m and storeys 3.55 and 3.1 m, the cornice line within about 10 px of the photograph's along the front

differences.what: the roof: very steep slate faces rising from the cornice to a flat deck ringed with cresting at about 16-19 m; the draft had a hip about 56 degrees off a 12 m eave
differences.how: T-2538: the builder's 72-degree mansard with a 7.2 m lower face and a low deck, its deck line within about 25 px of the photograph's; T-2843: a K05 mansard whose straight 72-degree faces hold two storeys (lower rise 7.2 m), a low tin deck over them; its faces within about 15 px of the photograph's and its peak about 1 m over the deck's line

differences.what: the south pavilion: three storeys of wall at the south end of the front under a steep coped stone gable, its apex about 17 m
differences.how: T-2538: part p_south, three storeys to 13.9 m under a 58-degree gable facing the avenue; its gable within about 30 px of the photograph's; T-2843: a K08 projection flush with the south corner, three storeys to 13.9 m with paired lights, its face within about 15 px of the photograph's x 1235-1345 (its gable is open below)

differences.what: the 18th Street flank: a three-storey section east of the tower and a gabled section beyond it, then a lower two-storey east range; the draft ran the whole flank at one height
differences.how: T-2538: parts p_flank and r3 at three storeys, r2 at two, eaves 13.9 and 8.1 m; T-2843: the section on a K08 projection to 13.9 m (6.0 m wide, against the tower), the gabled section and the east range as slated K01 wings at three and two storeys

differences.what: the east turret: a small round turret under a cone at the flank's north-east corner, its eaves about 8 m and its apex about 12.7 m; the draft had none
differences.how: T-2900: the photograph shows the turret's eaves level with the range's (about 8.0 m), a turret turned round the wing's corner; K08's tower on a wing's wall must stand 1.0 m past the wing's eave (T-2842), so the K01 build has none where the draft had one

differences.what: the corner entrance: an open loggia at the front's north-west corner, one round arch on each face, and a broad stair of about nine risers between curved cheek walls coming down the front; the build has a flat door and a straight stoop
differences.how: T-2910: a loggia behind two round arches, one on each face, each 1.9 m across centred 1.6 m from the corner and crowned 3.6 m (2.15 m over the 1.45 m floor) under a voussoir ring and keystone, within about 10 px of the photograph's arches; the room behind them with its double door in the back wall, seen through the 18th Street arch where the photograph shows the door frame; the stone balcony corbelled under the 18th Street arch; nine risers of 0.161 m coming down the front out of the front arch, 2.3 m broad, between cheeks that run level by the arch and sweep down to blocks at the foot, the foot within about 15 px of the photograph's

differences.what: the loggia's carving: the archivolts' mouldings, the carved piers and panels beside and over both arches, the carved blocks at the cheeks' foot and the balcony's carved face; the build lays them in plain stone under a voussoir ring

the bowed bay in the middle of the front, two storeys under a balcony, and the front's openings: paired and mullioned windows in carved surrounds, the carved frieze over the principal storey; the build has the draft's evenly spaced sash. The sheet's bulge (v 4.8-10.2) and the photograph's bay (about 60 px further north) disagree about where it stands
all-stone walls: Bedford stone laid in courses on the front and the flank alike, with string courses and the corbel table; the build is the draft's flat stand-in stone
differences.how: T-2843: an all-stone K01 house in K02's Bedford stone, coursed round every face; the string courses and the corbel table stay open under T-2790 and T-2540

differences.what: the tower's form: a shaft about 2.4 m across under a corbelled upper stage about 3.6 m across, its cone flaring from the stage; the build is one eight-sided prism 2.9 m across

the roof's dormers and deck: tall hooded dormers in the steep faces, the iron cresting and finials round the deck, the pavilion's and flank's tall stacks; the build's dormers sit sunk in the face and show only their gables, and it has no cresting
the gabled section on the flank: a gable facing 18th Street with a balcony at about 11.5 m; the build has a hip there
the south and east sides and the rear
differences.how: the camera looks from the north-west; T-2540 reads the HABS photographs for them

differences.what: colour: the stone's tone and the slate's

the south pavilion's coped stone gable over its third storey, its apex about 17 m with a carved panel and finial; the build caps the pavilion with K08's low hip at its 13.9 m wall top, where the draft had a steep gable
the main cornice: a heavy moulded stone cornice under the roof's faces; the build's eave is K05's plain fascia and soffit (K10's moulded stone cornice stands only under a flat or gable roof)

the pavilion and the flank section stand about 0-0.4 m proud on the sheet; the build stands both 0.6 m proud (K08's pavilion depth, the least its window recesses fit in), and the main eave dies behind their faces, and the flank section is 6.0 m wide (K08's widest) against the photograph's about 7.8 m, short of the gabled section
differences.how: L-kimball-1801-k01-2843; T-2540 reads the flank's sections

differences.what: the east range runs on south behind the gabled section to v 18.3 on the sheet; the build stops it at the gabled section's 6 m (a K01 wing stands inside its host wall); not seen from this camera
